subject: BrightCart launch: throughput commitment and mitigation checklist
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@brightcart.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Upcoming launch (May 3) - expected spike and quota request

Hi Priya,

Quick note from the launch team: our marketing blast is scheduled for May 3 and we expect a sharp 72-hour spike primarily during the first 8 hours post-send. Preliminary estimates show peak concurrent requests ~2.8x our current pilot usage and token volume ~3.1x daily average.

What we need from Redwood: a temporary quota uplift and a short runbook for throttling/fallback options in case of burst-induced latencies. Also, can you share any preferred patterns for prefix caching or batch sizing that BrightCart should follow to avoid unnecessary retries?

I attached our 72-hour projection (CSV). Happy to hop on a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Elena
Product Ops | BrightCart
[Attachment: brightcart_72hr_traffic_projection.csv (CSV)]

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morris <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming launch (May 3) - expected spike and quota request

Elena —

Thanks for the projection and heads up. I've looped in Rishi (runtime) and Connor (customer success/ingress ops) to validate the numbers and propose an uplift timeline. High-level notes from our side:

- We can provision a temporary quota increase for the launch window (May 3 00:00–May 6 23:59 PDT) to match your peak estimate, but we need a firm committed throughput target by EOD Friday so we can reserve capacity.
- Please confirm the ratio of short (<=64 token) vs long (>512 token) requests — this materially impacts kernel selection and memory pressure.
- We'll draft a short mitigation checklist (canary routing, 5xx escalation path, fallback model variant) and share as a mutual action plan.

Connor — can you add the proposed SLA exception steps and DocuSign links for the short-term uplift? Rishi — RQ on caching: do you want the prefix hashes or exact prompt buckets? We'll recommend exact prompt buckets where feasible.

Attaching a quick template for the mutual action plan; if you can sign off on throughput by Friday we can lock capacity.

— Priya
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: BC-mutual-action-plan.md (Markdown)]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming launch (May 3) - expected spike and quota request

Team —

I reviewed the CSV. A few technical clarifications before we commit:

- Peak QPS: CSV shows 4,200 qps at hour 3 of the spike, but average per-minute variance is high. Please confirm whether BrightCart will smooth client-side retries.
- Token mix: ~62% short requests, ~25% medium (128–512 tokens), ~13% long. If confirmed, we can route short requests to a low-latency pool with optimized kernels and keep long requests on a separate variant to avoid KV cache eviction thrash.
- Fallback model: recommend an explicit fallback variant (smaller quantized model) with 20% capacity reserved in case of memory pressure. That gives us breathing room while keeping quality acceptable.

Action items for BrightCart: confirm smoothing policy and provide example of the most common short prompt (we'll use for prefix aggregation).

Rishi
Sr. Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morris <elena@brightcart.com>, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 14:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming launch (May 3) - expected spike and quota request

Hi Elena / Priya —

We put together a mutual action plan and a short throughput checklist:

1) Committed numbers: please confirm a firm peak qps and a hard token/day cap for May 3–6. We recommend committing to 4,200 qps peak based on your projection so we can reserve Dedicated slots.
2) Temporary uplift: REDWOOD will provision a temporary quota increase (policy change) effective 2027-05-03T00:00 to 2027-05-06T23:59 PDT.
3) Mitigations we will enact if latency > 250ms p50 or 500ms p95 for more than 10 minutes:
   - Canary route 10% traffic to fallback quantized variant
   - Throttle non-essential batch jobs and background calls
   - Activate cross-region fallback to us-west-2 with reduced token caps
4) Operational touches: DocuSign link for the temporary uplift is: https://docusign.company/BC-Uplift-46392. HubSpot record HS-46392 updated with notes.

Please reply to this thread with a single-line confirmation of: (a) agreed peak qps, (b) token cap, and (c) whether you accept the mitigation checklist. Once confirmed, we'll submit the capacity reservation and send the DocuSign.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morris <elena@brightcart.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightCart Ops <ops@brightcart.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 17:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming launch (May 3) - expected spike and quota request

Connor / Priya —

Confirmed. BrightCart accepts the proposed plan.

(a) Peak qps: 4,250 (we'll cap retries client-side)
(b) Token cap (May 3–6): 1,200,000 tokens/day
(c) Mitigation checklist: accepted — we will add a short client-side TTL to reduce duplicate requests.

Connor, I'll sign the DocuSign later today. Thanks to the team for the speedy coordination.

Best,
Elena
Product Ops | BrightCart
